transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~37 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Cardinal CISO), Marcus Bennett (Cardinal Head Eng), Aisha Khan (Cardinal Compliance)

Summary: quick readout of what's in scope for SOC2/ISO handoff, how they get access to our trust center, and a KMS/key rotation discussion. Also some mapping questions around RBAC roles and audit logs.

Topics: SOC2 report, ISO certs, Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO mapping, audit logs retention/export, KMS integration, data residency, next steps/POC.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, can everyone hear me ok?
00:05 Leah: yes loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:20 Maya: awesome, so high level today we'll walk through what we can share for SOC 2 and ISO, how you get into our Trust Center, and then Omar will dig into RBAC, SSO flows and KMS bits. We're targeting this to be a posture readout, not a deep tech demo, but we'll schedule deeper follow ups.
00:42 Marcus: sounds good. Just flagging up front — our audit team needs the full controls mapping not just a summary, so we'll want a CSV or something we can ingest.
00:52 Maya: totally, we'll hand the CSV and the mapping; Omar will run through the fields.
01:10 Omar: hi all, quick intro — I'm Omar on infra and can take the technical Qs. One thing to note, sometimes the auto-transcripts call KV cash instead of KV cache — just a heads up, you'll see small typos in the documents.
01:30 Aisha: ha noted. On the SOC2, do you have the Type II for the last 12 months available?
01:38 Maya: yes we do. We can share the June 2026 SOC 2 Type II PDF. It's scoped to hosted + dedicated endpoints but excludes on-prem offline packages — we call that 'private' in the docs.
01:55 Leah: and ISO?
01:57 Maya: ISO 27001 cert is available — cover page and scope page included. We'll also share the Statement of Applicability as an artifact.
02:10 Marcus: good. For the Trust Center, what's the minimum permission set so our audit team can download evidence? We don't want to give full admin.
02:20 Omar: the Trust Center has role-based viewers: viewer, auditor, admin. Viewer can see redacted artifacts, auditor can download signed PDFs with metadata, admin can manage invites. We usually recommend auditor role for external audit teams.
02:40 Leah: is that integrated with our SSO? We use Okta and need SCIM for provisioning if possible.
02:48 Maya: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. We'll need your SAML metadata and optionally a SCIM endpoint for automatic user provisioning. If you don't want SCIM we can invite users manually.
03:10 Leah: ok we'll prefer SCIM. We'll provide the SAML metadata.
03:20 Aisha: on evidence, how granular are the artifacts? Is it per-control PDF or bundles? Our process wants each control evidence file.
03:30 Omar: we provide both. The Trust Center groups artifacts by control ID, you can download per-control evidence bundles (PDFs, logs, screenshots) and there's also an export CSV that maps Redwood control IDs to the SOC framework IDs.
03:46 Marcus: what about audit logs? Format, retention, and export — we need syslog/ELK friendly formats.
03:55 Omar: logs are JSON lines, fields include timestamp, user_id (pseudonymized for hosted), resource_id, action, region, and request_id. Retention defaults to 13 months for enterprise tiers, can be extended to 36 months as an add-on. We can stream those logs to a customer S3 with SSE-KMS or to a SIEM via our forwarder.
04:20 Leah: streaming to S3 with SSE-KMS is preferred. We have a KMS policy requirement where our keys must be customer-managed. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
04:32 Maya: yes, we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys. For hosted flows you can bring-your-own KMS (BYOK). For Dedicated we recommend using a customer KMS in the same cloud account; for Private on-prem we'll support HSM integrations.
04:47 Aisha: how do you handle key rotation — do you require downtime?
04:52 Omar: rotation is seamless — we use envelope encryption. You rotate the data encryption key in KMS, and Redwood's runtime will fetch the new DEK and re-encrypt metadata as needed. There's no scheduled downtime but we recommend coordinating rotation windows for audit records.
05:15 Marcus: any constraints around cross-region keys or do keys have to live in the same region as data?
05:21 Omar: keys must be in the same cloud region for low-latency decryption in our default config, but technically we can support cross-region keys with an accepted latency tradeoff. That is usually a design decision for residency-sensitive customers.
05:40 Leah: residency — our legal requires EU-only residency for EU customers. Can we pin data to eu-west-1?
05:46 Maya: yes, we support region binding for data at rest. For hosted we have EU regions; we can route requests and store embeddings and logs in eu-west-1. For Dedicated we'd provision GPU capacity in that region.
06:05 Aisha: excellent. On RBAC, we need a mapping to our internal roles. Do you have a prebuilt mapping matrix?
06:12 Omar: yes, there is a mapping template — Owner, Admin, Auditor, Developer, ReadOnly. We'll share the template. It includes SAML attributes we use for role assertions (roles, groups). Our mapping supports group-to-role and attribute-based claims.
06:30 Marcus: what about API tokens? We want token scoping and short-lived tokens for services.
06:36 Omar: tokens can be short-lived with TTLs as low as 15 minutes, and you can issue service tokens with scopes (generate, embeddings, admin). We recommend using our session-based tokens with rotation via your CI/CD.
06:55 Leah: for the control mapping, we need to see how each control maps to our policy names and evidence owners. How do you typically format that CSV?
07:05 Maya: the CSV will include columns: redwood_control_id, description, framework (SOC2/ISO), evidence_type, evidence_location, last_updated, contact_owner. We'll fill the initial mapping and leave contact_owner blank for you to populate.
07:26 Aisha: any known gaps customers should expect?
07:30 Omar: most customers ask about on-prem evidence for private deployments — the hosted trust center doesn't include local host-level logs for private. If you plan on private on-prem deployment, we ship a different evidence bundle that includes host logs if collection is enabled.
07:50 Marcus: ok makes sense. Can you also share the changelog for the last 6 months — we want to see control changes and major infra updates.
07:58 Maya: yes we'll include a high-level change log and a link to release notes. We'll annotate any changes that impact compliance posture.
08:12 Leah: quick question — do you support certificate transparency or are TLS certs managed by you? We need proof certs are rotated every 90 days.
08:20 Omar: TLS certs for hosted endpoints are managed by Redwood with automation; rotation is every 60 to 90 days depending on CA. We can provide the cert rotation schedule and signed cert snapshots.
08:40 Aisha: on the Trust Center invite — can you make a temporary auditor account for our external auditor? They will need to download the evidence bundle next week.
08:48 Maya: yes, provision auditor role. Leah, if you send the auditor email addresses and SAML metadata, we can add them as auditor and set expirations on the invites.
09:02 Leah: we'll send that today.
09:08 Marcus: one more item — PII tagging and redaction in logs. Do you redact PII in audit logs automatically?
09:16 Omar: by default we pseudonymize user identifiers for hosted multi-tenant flows. For Dedicated we can opt into full user ids if you want. There's also a redaction pipeline that strips specific fields — we can configure that for you.
09:36 Leah: great. On evidence delivery, do you have a secure transfer for large artifacts? We need SHA256 hashes for integrity checks.
09:44 Maya: Trust Center artifacts are checksum-signed and we provide sha256 values on each download. For large sets we can also arrange an S3 transfer with signed URLs and object versioning.
10:02 Aisha: let's talk timeline — our audit window is mid-November, so we need completed mapping and access by end of September to avoid last-minute churn.
10:12 Maya: that aligns fine; our target will be to get the CSV and Trust Center access by 2026-09-20 so you have weeks to review.
10:25 Marcus: can we also schedule the private deployment latency check? We want to verify 99th percentile token latency for our model mix.
10:33 Omar: yes, I'll set up a small bench — synthetic traces with your sequence lengths. We'll need a sample prompt set and expected QPS.
10:44 Marcus: I'll send the prompt set and expected QPS today.
10:50 Maya: perfect. Quick recap — action items: Maya share SOC2/ISO artifacts and Trust Center link, Omar share control mapping CSV and plan for latency check, Leah provide SAML metadata and auditor emails. We'll target the dates in the action items.
11:12 Leah: sounds good. Thanks everyone.
11:20 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the links and the CSV. End call.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'Trustcenter' combined), names sometimes appear as partial; manual review recommended before feeding into compliance trackers.
